outline.title: Decision Control Plane
outline.summary: The concrete product that turns the Decision Infrastructure theory into a dependable first release: a financial-crime screening control plane.

outline.title: What we are making
outline.summary: Define the product promise: a fast, governed, replayable answer to whether a high-consequence transaction may proceed.

outline.title: The first wedge is financial-crime screening
outline.summary: Show why transaction screening is the right proving ground: it stresses identity, time, policy, action, audit, and resilience at once.

outline.title: System architecture: three planes, one decision artifact
outline.summary: Present the detailed Decision Control Plane architecture using the rendered component diagram.

outline.title: One transaction, end to end
outline.summary: Present the component interaction sequence from transaction proposal through policy evaluation, action acknowledgement, audit, and reassessment.

outline.title: The kernel stays small and stable
outline.summary: Separate the invariant Decision Kernel from the AML Domain Adapter and replaceable engines.

outline.title: The minimum valuable product
outline.summary: Show the complete vertical slice that must work before broader platform ambitions are funded.

outline.title: The 90-day MVP validation plan
outline.summary: Present the four validation gates and the evidence required to proceed, narrow, or stop.

outline.title: Success is measured in proof, not activity
outline.summary: Present the metrics and hard thresholds for replay, audit, latency, resilience, operational value, and reuse.

outline.title: The stress test changes the architecture
outline.summary: Show the exact bottleneck result: audit commit saturates before the Policy Interpreter, so durable logging must scale independently.

outline.title: Build the kernel before the platform
outline.summary: Close with the staged roadmap and RoR-based sequencing from falsifiers to productization.
